This PR reverses the documented tie-break rule just to make one test pass. The docstring says tied quotients go to the team with the LARGER headcount. The PR uses `-headcounts[team]`, so ties go to the SMALLER team, and the description calls that "fairer." The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, so the code shouldn't do the opposite of what they say.

The reason is `test_quarterly_floor_plan` (platform 60, design 30, support 16, 6 desks). If you follow the docstring, desk 2 is a 30/30 tie that goes to platform, and desk 6 is a 15/15 tie that also goes to platform. That gives {platform: 4, design: 1, support: 1}, but the test expects {3, 2, 1}. So the test and the docstring disagree. The other tests don't depend on this: test_larger_floor has no ties.

These parts are good and should stay: the ValueError checks, starting every team at 0, and using Fraction for exact comparison. Please put back the `+headcounts[team]` tie-break key. Then tell the teammate that test_quarterly_floor_plan contradicts the documented rule, and let them decide whether to fix the test or the spec. Don't quietly change the behaviour.
